_notes: Penetration of a projectile at close range (muzzle to about 100 m), at normal incidence, in millimetres of: steel = RHA-equivalent (about 300 HB); concrete = unreinforced structural concrete; brick = fired clay brick masonry; wood = dry hardwood (oak). A game scales it by the energy left at the hit (shotToHit does).

basis 'published' = taken from a manufacturer figure quoted in sources. basis 'estimated' = our estimate from published orders of magnitude (ball ammunition defeats 4 to 6 mm of RHA, steel-core 6 to 8 mm, AP 10 to 22 mm, .50 BMG ball about 14 mm), muzzle energy and bullet construction; the concrete, brick and wood columns scale with penetrator energy and hardness the way test firings against masonry and timber do. They are meant to be refined with datasheets: override any entry with ArsenalOptions.ammo / patch.ammo.

Anchors: Nammo 7.62 mm x 51 Armor Piercing 8 (M993): 18 mm RHA at 100 m, 7 mm at 500 m (https://www.nammo.com/products/ammunition/small-caliber-ammunition/7-62mm-series/7-62-mm-x-51-armor-piercing-8-m993/). Constructions (M80 lead core with gilding-metal jacket, M43 and 7N6 steel cores, M995 and M993 tungsten carbide, M33 lead with steel insert, M2 hardened steel, BZ and B-32 steel core API) follow the usual military ammunition references (TM 43-0001-27, Army small-arms ammunition tables).

core: lead, lead_steel (lead with a steel tip or insert), steel, hardened_steel, tungsten_carbide, copper, none. jacket: gilding_metal, copper, brass, steel (copper-washed or lacquered steel), none. They only feed the ignition rules (rules.ignition.spark).
bulletGrams and muzzleSpeed, when present, replace those of the calibre for this load; absent they are the calibre's.
